client_brief:
Forecourt cards for current stock, with honest paint and highlight handling

Vanguard Motors has fourteen cars on the forecourt, but the feed still includes vehicles sold or reserved. Please reconcile the stock before producing the A4 window cards. The photography also needs care: some panels were overexposed during the shoot.

This is the required package:

A4 portrait, one vehicle per page in feed order, page count equal to the count of cars actually on the forecourt with sold and reserved units excluded by record range, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every card binds year, marque, model, derivative, mileage, colour, the nine-item spec block, price and the finance wording verbatim from the feed, plus that car's own photograph in the correct graphic frame. Accompanied by one single-vehicle file per car named to its stock number and identity-verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived.

Eighteen supplied frames reconciled to fourteen vehicles and brought to one house white and one black point across two lighting sessions, paint colour honest on every car, delivered as one card window and one wider lot picture per vehicle at a consistent vehicle scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. No bodywork invented anywhere. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, the outcome of every highlight recovery attempt recorded, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

Finance wording and the nine-item specification block must come through exactly as supplied. Keep the car's actual paint colour, and record the outcome of each highlight-recovery attempt. Do not invent bodywork where the exposure contains no detail.

Available: lot_photos/ (18 frames, 5200 x 3400); windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf; stock_feed.csv; forecourt_plate.jpg (3800 x 2600); finance_wording.txt; forecourt_photo.jpg.

Please check the individual stock-number files by opening them, and leave the recovered live template with its derivation notes. We need to trust both the printed card and the reusable process.

$3,000-$7,000 fixed; 2 to 4 weeks. Review structure: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the recurring dealership brief posted on Upwork and Freelancer.com, 'window cards / forecourt spec cards for our stock, one per vehicle, from our stock feed', where the dealer supplies a spreadsheet exported from the stock management system carrying registration, stock number, price, mileage and a spec block, plus a folder of photographs taken on the lot, and asks for a printed card per car so the forecourt stops looking like a collection of handwritten prices. Co-anchor: the equally common 'we only have the PDF our printer made' brief, where the working file is gone and the client's standing instruction is to keep the card exactly as it is and put this month's stock through it, with named single-vehicle files needed because a card is reprinted the day a car sells. The ledger records this slot (LAYOUT-B-14) as a record-per-page merge with a per-vehicle photo column, one_line_ask 'so every car on the lot displays a consistent branded card', and the triage verdict is STRENGTHEN: the concept, the collateral set and the price-band logic are right, but as banked the engagement sat almost entirely on the merge surface with the lot photography and the dealership's own mark treated as plumbing. LAYOUT-32 keeps the concept and the deliverables and restores the commission the dealer actually posts: the photography has to be fixed because it was shot in one bright overcast morning, the shield has to be recovered because the only clean version left is the plate above the office door, and the point of fixing both is that the window cards, the forecourt board and the Monday sales meeting all come out of one stock list and have to agree. All vehicle marques and models named in the engagement are coined; no real manufacturer, dealer group, finance house or regulator appears.

price_band_and_audience: Vehicles from 18,000 pounds (a low-mileage compact estate, a four-year-old hatchback) to 95,000 pounds (a two-year-old grand tourer, a specification-heavy performance saloon). Buyer 35 to 60, a private retail buyer who has already narrowed the choice online, has driven a distance to see one specific car, and is deciding whether this dealer is careful. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is photograph forward and quiet: one large honest picture of the actual car, a short specification of the things that differ between examples, the price present and plainly set rather than shouted, the finance line legible and secondary, and generous space. Push it toward the budget lot register, the monthly payment set enormous, a burst badge, a saturated red price flash, three exclamation points of specification, and a 95,000 pound car reads as a car with something wrong with it, which is the exact commercial failure this dealer is paying to avoid. Push it the other way into a manufacturer-style brochure with no price and no mileage and the card stops doing the one job it has, which is answering the two questions a buyer has while standing in the rain. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,600 to 3,200 pounds fixed, or 45 to 70 pounds an hour across 30 to 45 hours.

brand_identity.sector: An independent prestige used vehicle dealership selling to retail buyers and part exchange customers from a single forecourt.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2006, one forecourt in Harrogate, North Yorkshire. A small independent holding about fourteen cars at a time, buying selectively rather than to volume.
brand_identity.about: Vanguard holds around fourteen carefully bought cars at a time and sells to people who have already decided roughly what they want and are choosing where to buy it. The card in the windscreen is the first thing a buyer meets, before anyone walks out, so it has to answer their two questions honestly: what is this car, and what does it cost.
brand_identity.audience: Private retail buyers aged 35 to 60 who have narrowed the choice online, driven a distance to see one specific car, and are deciding whether this dealer is careful.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent prestige used. Cars from 18,000 pounds to 95,000. Photograph forward and quiet: one large honest picture of the actual car, a short spec of what differs between examples, the price plainly set and the finance line legible but secondary. Never the budget lot register, never a manufacturer brochure with no price.
brand_identity.typography: A confident low contrast serif or sturdy grotesque for the marque and headline, paired with a clean neutral sans for the spec block, price and finance footer. Careful and quiet, neither discount loud nor brochure sparse.
brand_identity.voice: Factual, unhurried and confident, a dealer who lets the car and the spec do the talking. No exclamation, no urgency. Example: One owner, full history, the colour it says on the card and the colour it is on the forecourt.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The shield artwork is long gone. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the pressed and painted aluminium plate above the office door, weathered by several winters, carrying the shield at about 180mm. The current stock, specs and prices arrive from the stock feed, and the finance wording is fixed by the broker.
brand_identity.values: Cars bought with care and sold without spin, and a forecourt where the card and the vehicle always agree.

assets_supplied.name: lot_photos/ (18 frames, 5200 x 3400)
assets_supplied.kind: The dealer's own photography of fourteen vehicles taken on the forecourt across one bright overcast morning and one late afternoon, handheld, with a few alternate wider frames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole lot in one morning, the last few late on. The silver and white ones have gone to nothing on the screen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The white and silver cars' bonnets and roofs and the sky behind them are genuinely clipped rather than merely bright, so a highlight recovery on those frames returns an image visually identical to the one that went in while reporting complete success, and no response says the data was not there. Separately, three vehicles were shot so tight that the card's landscape window cannot be taken from them without cutting the front wing, and the crop tool responds by offering an expand chain that would fabricate bodywork on a car a buyer will stand in front of.

assets_supplied.name: windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of the current window card, A4 portrait, one vehicle per page, fonts embedded, produced from the dealer's old system through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries the shield, a vehicle photograph, a headline, a two-column spec block, the price and the finance footer.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sent us two seasons ago. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The conversion returns nothing like the structure the printed page suggests. The tidy two-column spec block, the price line and the finance footer all arrive as ONE continuous tab-delimited story that has to be driven by ordered offsets, while the single-looking headline splits into three separate frames because year, marque and model were placed as separate runs, and the two graphic frames (the vehicle photograph and the shield) are distinguishable only by their bounds and their link, neither being named for what it holds.

assets_supplied.name: stock_feed.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the dealership's stock management system, one row per unit, with columns for stock number, registration, marque, model, derivative, year, mileage, colour, transmission, fuel, a nine-item spec block, price, monthly figure, status and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Straight out of the system on Monday morning. The prices are what we are asking today."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Seventeen rows for fourteen cars actually on the forecourt: three sold or reserved units the system still emits, flagged only by a status column the dealer never mentions. Stock numbers have lost their leading zeros to the spreadsheet that exported them, one car's mileage cell is empty, two derivative names run four times the length of the rest because the clerk pasted the full factory description, prices sit as raw integers with no separators or currency, and the image column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, so a naive run binds one car's photograph to every card or binds none at all.

assets_supplied.name: forecourt_plate.jpg (3800 x 2600)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the pressed and painted aluminium plate above the office door carrying the Vanguard Motors shield at about 180mm wide, weathered by several winters, shot in flat daylight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean version of the shield we have. The artwork went years ago."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The shield is a bordered device with an enclosed chevron counter and a hairline keyline inside the outer edge, and the plate's weathering means the trace comes back carrying near-identical greys as separate fills and slightly broken edges along that keyline. It reads perfectly at inspection scale and on white, and the card reproduces it at roughly a fifth of the plate's size on a deep midnight ground.

assets_supplied.name: finance_wording.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The wording the dealership's finance broker requires on any printed material carrying a monthly figure, 310 characters, supplied as plain text.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This has to appear on every card that shows a monthly payment, word for word, and it is not ours to change."

assets_supplied.name: forecourt_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Phone snap of the forecourt and the entrance board, supplied as a feel reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the forecourt. The board is by the gate."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether there is anything left to recover in the blown areas. The dealer describes the bonnets and roofs of the white and silver cars as gone, which reads as an exposure complaint, and the natural response is a highlight recovery pass. On these particular frames the readout is that nothing moves: the call succeeds, returns an image, and the recovered file is visually indistinguishable from the one that went in, because those pixels are genuinely clipped rather than merely bright. Nothing in any response says so. Which frames are recoverable and which are not is a property of these exposures and cannot be known from the dealer's description, from the previews (a bright roof and a clipped roof look the same on screen) or from the session split, because two afternoon frames recover fully and three morning frames do not.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the only way to learn whether the data survived is to attempt the recovery and compare the result against the input, and the tool reports success in both cases. Nothing states it: the brief says the panels have gone to nothing, which is a client describing a symptom, and no asset description names which vehicles are unrecoverable. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to change what the picture is rather than to redo the correction, which reopens the crop policy and the treatment decision for the affected cars.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each recovery result against its input rather than accepting the call, then handle the unrecoverable frames a different way: re-frame from an alternate wider frame where one exists so less clipped sky is carried, re-decide the card window crop so the blown roof sits outside it, or, where neither works, escalate that the car needs rephotographing rather than shipping a card with a hole in the bodywork. Then re-judge white point and vehicle scale across all fourteen, because cars re-framed for a different reason will not sit with the rest unless the policy is re-taken as a set.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A forecourt of cards on which the most expensive white and silver cars have a featureless white hole where the bonnet and roof should be, printed and put in the windscreens of the actual vehicles, by a dealer whose entire pitch is that he is careful.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually is underneath. The printed page shows a tidy two-column spec block, one price line, one footer, one headline and one photograph, and every sensible plan maps those as separate frames. The conversion returns the opposite shape: the spec block, the price and the finance footer arrive as one continuous tab-delimited story that can only be driven by ordered offsets, while the single-looking headline splits into three separate frames because year, marque and model were placed as separate runs, and the two graphic frames carry no name, only bounds and a link, so which one holds the vehicle photograph and which holds the shield is not stated anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity from a PDF is not a parameter, is not reported before conversion and has no read-ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export IDML and read, and the shape it returns is the inverse of the one the printed page implies. Nothing states it: the brief says only to keep the card as it is and put the current stock through it, and names no frames, stories or fields. It is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping strategy itself changes, from per-field frames to two different strategies inside one card, and the image binding has to be settled by rendering a page rather than by reading the response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Discard the planned per-field map. Reconstruct the true story from the IDML content runs, compute offsets against that string for everything in the body, map the three headline frames individually by their integer page-item ids, and settle the photograph's frame by rendering one record and reading it against the printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the photograph. Then rebuild, re-validate, re-prepare and re-verify the placeholders before any card is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A template that validates and reports success while binding the model into the year's frame and the vehicle photograph into the shield's frame, producing fourteen cards that are confidently wrong in the two places a buyer looks first.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered shield survives its own reproduction. Traced off a 180mm pressed plate it is immaculate at inspection scale and on a white ground, and it carries perfectly onto the A1 entrance panel. The window card reproduces it at roughly a fifth of that size on the card's deep midnight ground, and at that size on that ground the hairline keyline and the enclosed chevron counter fill in and the shield reads as a solid lozenge, while the plate's weathering, which was invisible as texture, shows as broken edges. This cannot be judged from the trace, from the SVG on screen or from the A1, because it is a product of the reproduction size, the ink behaviour of the card's dark ground and the specific edge quality this particular trace inherited from a weathered plate.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the artwork is genuinely correct at every size it is inspected at until it is rendered at true trim on the real ground, and no tool reports a reproduction limit. Nothing states it: the brief says the shield is on the cards and the board, and never asks how small it can go, so nothing has already discovered it. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to author a different piece of artwork for the small dark application rather than to re-place the same one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Produce a reproduction cut of the shield for the card: reduce the trace to the marks that survive at card size, open or drop the hairline keyline, keep the chevron counter open, and consolidate the weathering greys into flat fills, then re-generate the raster plate the merge binds, re-merge and re-render, and check it again at true trim on the dark ground rather than on screen. Keep the full-detail artwork for the A1 panel and record in the handover which version belongs where and below what size the detailed one stops holding.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen window cards and every sold slip carrying a shield that has closed into an unreadable dark blob, on the one element that appears on every printed thing this dealership owns, delivered as a recovered brand asset.

decision_gates: The surface split: window cards to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is record per page, forecourt set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which session sets the house white, knowing a late-afternoon reference makes every silver car on the lot look warm.
Whether a highlight recovery actually recovered anything, on frames where the response looks the same either way.

What to do with a car whose card window cannot be taken without cutting it: a different frame, a different crop policy, or an honest escalation, given that the expand chain would fabricate bodywork on a car the buyer will stand in front of.
Whether the card photograph is the car in its forecourt context or the car lifted onto a graded ground, decided against the printer's own dark card rather than against the screen.
Vehicle scale across the set, decided as a forecourt rather than per car, and re-decided once any car is re-framed for a different reason.
How to name the selection that recovers the shield: naming the plate pulls the aluminium, naming the painted device's own colour and form pulls the mark.

Whether the traced shield is artwork or merely output, including the backing path that rides along, the weathering carried as separate fills, and whether one cut can serve both an A1 panel and a small dark card.

Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.
Paint colour is honest on every car, and no correction has moved a silver toward blue, a white toward cream or a black into crush. A colour a buyer would dispute on arrival is a rejected picture.

verifiers_human.text: Laid out together, the fourteen cars read as one forecourt photographed on one morning at one vehicle scale.
No card window cuts the front or rear of the vehicle, and no bodywork anywhere has been invented.
Paint colour is honest on every car, with no silver pushed blue, no white pushed cream and no black crushed shut.
The shield still reads as the shield at the size it is printed on the card, on the card's own dark ground.

The collateral reads photograph forward and quiet, appropriate to an 18,000 to 95,000 pound car and a buyer who has already narrowed the choice, rather than budget-lot loud or manufacturer-brochure silent.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and this folder into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of cars. IDENTITY: these are fourteen specific vehicles, each with a registration, a stock number, a mileage and a paint colour that a buyer has driven forty miles to see, and a generated car fabricates a wheel, a badge, a trim level or a colour, which on a card that also carries a price is a false claim about the goods. The dealership shield is a specific pressed device that must come back as the same shield, because it is already on the board at the gate. SPEC: the dealer needs one card per car actually on the forecourt at A4 and 300 ppi with every value bound verbatim from their own stock feed, sold and reserved units absent, the full finance wording present word for word, each card carrying its own photograph, and one separately named file per stock number containing the car its filename claims. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next week's stock is a data change, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork so prices can move every week. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did anything survive in that blown roof, did this placeholder get created, is this photograph in the photograph's frame, does this shield still read at card size. That is not a generation problem.
